lines.li: [us] Why do the Wardens carry lanterns in broad daylight?
[them] For Tobin Garrow, a shepherd whose village was emptied in one night.
[us] What emptied it?
[them] Something out of the treeline, so he lit his dead brother's lantern at the crossroads.
[us] For how long?
[them] Eleven years, until it was dead, and those who walked with him were the first of us.
[them] Every lodge keeps a book, with a page for every beast we've run down.
[us] And the empty pages?
[them] Those are for the ones still loose, and every page of the book gets its ending.
[us] What's on the cord on your sleeve?
[them] A knot for every beast felled, and you count the knots, not the years.
[us] What does a Warden fear?
[them] The beast that gets away, and a crossroads with no light at it.
[us] Not dying on a hunt?
[them] Dying with an empty page behind me, that's worse.
[us] Do you hunt everything that moves?
[them] Only the ones that take people, and the pelts pay for the lantern oil.
[us] How do you tell which ones?
[them] Follow the lanterns, a beast that takes a person answers for it.
[us] Why does the Bell bury even raiders?
[them] Nobody would bury the raiders after the long war, and what came up taught us better.
[us] Who started it?
[them] A widow called Ysolde Marr, with a spade and a cracked chapel bell.
[us] What did she do with the bell?
[them] Rang it once over every grave, friend or foe, until the ground was quiet.
[them] Everyone is owed a bell.
[us] Even the ones who came over our wall?
[them] Those most of all, and those who did the killing owe the burying.
[us] That's a hard thing to ask.
[them] The ground doesn't ask, it only keeps what it is given.
[us] Does anything frighten the Bell?
[them] The unburied dead, and a field that stirs at night.
[us] Stirs?
[them] Bury them deep, and listen, and you won't have to find out.
[us] Isn't it grim work, digging all day?
[them] It's quiet work, and somebody ought to do it kindly.
[us] Do you ever get used to it?
[them] You get used to the digging, never to the bell.
[us] How did the Circuit start?
[them] A herder girl called Nessa Pell found an egg in the crater a falling star had made.
[us] What hatched?
[them] Nobody agrees, but she walked forty years with it and challenged every tamer she met.
[us] And she won?
[them] Mostly, and the Circuit grew from those she beat and those who beat her.
[them] Every token on this sash is a bout I won fairly.
[us] What's the highest honour a tamer can have?
[them] To be beaten fairly by a stranger, believe it or not.
[us] Why would you want to lose?
[them] Because then there's someone better on the road, and I get to learn from them.
[us] What does a tamer hate most?
[them] A leash, and a beast ill-used by someone who calls that training.
[us] And losing?
[them] Losing's fine, a bout won by a trick is what I can't stand.
[us] How do you train them to fight like that?
[them] You don't train them, you win their trust and they win your battles.
[us] That sounds slower.
[them] A bond is not a leash, and it lasts a great deal longer.
[us] Why does the Wheel never stop?
[them] The night our valley burned, Mab Wainwright put her house on her cart and drove out.
[us] And everyone followed?
[them] With whatever they could lift, and nobody has ever voted to stop.
[us] Has anyone tried?
[them] Every few years someone stands up, and by then we've already moved on.
[them] Nothing is broken, only waiting.
[us] Waiting for what?
[them] For somebody who can be bothered to mend it, and that's us.
[us] Why the brass cog on every shoulder?
[them] Because nothing on the Wheel is thrown away, least of all a person.
[us] What's the Wheel afraid of?
[them] Standing still, and the fire behind us.
[us] Isn't the fire long out?
[them] That's what people say right before it catches them.
[us] Who buys rubbish?
[them] We do, and then we sell it back to you better.
[us] That can't be much of a living.
[them] Buy it cheap, sell it better, and you'd be surprised.
